Null thresholds of pooled scores

Source: R/caller.R
pooled_thresholds.Rd

Null pools are built with the same construction as the test pools (pools_fun, e.g. random pools within cell type of null cells, or kNN pools of null cells), scored per pool x region, and the type-7 q quantile is taken per by (class). Random constructions are redrawn (seed + draw) until every class has at least n_draws null pool-regions; a deterministic construction (same pools twice, e.g. kNN) is used once. With cv one threshold per fold from the null cells of the other folds, plus fold 0 from all null cells. With loo the leave-one-out scores (s_rob) are computed and can be thresholded, exactly as call_pools() scores the test pools.

Usage

pooled_thresholds(
  d_null,
  pools_fun,
  n_draws = 20000,
  by = "class",
  q = params$null_q,
  cv = TRUE,
  states = caller_states("normal", params),
  scores = c("s_depth", "s_allelic", "s_comb", if (loo) "s_rob"),
  params = caller_defaults(),
  max_draws = 200,
  loo = FALSE,
  standardize = FALSE,
  min_region_pools = 1000
)

Arguments

d_null

null rows scored with keep_rows = TRUE (cell, region, class, fold)

pools_fun

function(cells, seed) returning a pools table (pool, cell)

n_draws

minimal null pool-regions per class

by

grouping of the thresholds; with sexgrp (autosome / X / Y, caller_normal() for males with pool_sex_thr), a group with fewer than min_region_pools null pool-regions takes the class threshold (pooled_fallback), and redraws are counted per class

q

null quantile

cv

per-fold thresholds

states

state set used for scoring

scores

pooled scores to threshold

params

caller_defaults()

max_draws

maximal redraws

loo

leave-one-out scores (adds s_rob to the default scores)

standardize

standardise the pooled best LLR per region (pool_scale() of the fold's null pools) before thresholding; the fold-0 scale is returned as attribute pool_scale (pass it to call_pools()). With params$pool_tail_q > 0 the scale carries the per-region tail factor (tail_k = params$pool_tail_k, n_eff = the fold's null cells / params$n_pool). With params$pool_tail_xfit (default) the tail is cross-fitted: the fold's null cells are split in two halves (seeded), pools are built within each half (n_draws / 2 and min_region_pools / 2 each), each half's pools are standardised by the other half's scale before the quantile, and the returned scale is the mean of the two half scales (geometric mean of the tails)

min_region_pools

with standardize, random constructions are redrawn until every region also has this many null pools (a stable median / MAD per region; fewer pools make the in-sample standardised threshold anti-conservative)

Value

thresholds table (stratum "all"; n_null = null pool-regions); with standardize, attribute pool_scale
